allow_large: The owner allowed it: five code files plus the agent guide the review rule requires
done_when: At most 2 Forge agent runs (forge work rounds, plan reads and close reviews) run at once on one machine across all repos; the others wait in line first come, first served and print one plain line with their place when they start waiting and each time it changes; a run that dies frees its place; the guide says so. A command-level test starts three runs with stub agents and shows the third waits until one ends, then runs.

findings.body: The prior Codex crash finding remains open: this records only the driver's identity, not the app-server's. tests/test_fix_leftover_app_server_bare_command.py:28–33 explicitly kills Forge and its driver and verifies that the app-server survives. machine.py:69 then removes that reservation because both recorded owners are dead. Runs from other repos can fill both slots while the orphaned agent still consumes memory, exceeding the promised limit. Track the app-server or process-group lifetime until the actual agent ends.
findings.title: Not done: At most 2 Forge agent runs (forge work rounds, plan reads and close reviews) run at once on one machine across all repos

findings.body: The prior interruption finding remains open: SIGINT directed at Forge unwinds review.py:535–547 without terminating or waiting for Autoreview, but this finally block unconditionally removes its reservation. cli.py:123–124 then exits Forge, allowing a replacement alongside the surviving review. Sibling paths worker.py:497–506 and story.py:681–685 also release prematurely: [CPython 3.11's Popen context manager](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.11.11/Lib/subprocess.py#L993-L1018) only waits briefly on KeyboardInterrupt and does not terminate the child. Preserve reservations for surviving agents across all three paths, or terminate and reap them before releasing their slots.
findings.title: Keep reservations until interrupted agents have actually ended

findings.body: The prior launch-registration finding remains open. Autoreview starts at review.py:531–532 with the prompt already in argv and no launch handshake. If Forge dies before started() finishes writing the child's identity, its reservation still has agent=None. machine.py:69 removes that entry even though Autoreview is running, admitting a replacement beyond the two-agent ceiling. Gate execution on durable ownership or make the child retain its reservation independently of Forge.
findings.title: Prevent review execution before its ownership is durably recorded

findings.body: The prior test gap remains open. This test exercises normal completion with one waiter and Claude for both work and read; tests/test_close.py:229 and tests/conftest.py:176–179 confirm those adapter choices. It cannot detect reordered admission, missing position-change messages, broken crash release, or removal of Codex's read/work admission guards. Existing close-test queue tests exercise a separate mechanism, and Codex crash tests do not assert the machine-wide ceiling. Extend command-level coverage with multiple waiters, controlled deaths and both adapters, checking order, changed positions and actual live-agent counts.
findings.title: Not done: Command-level proof of FIFO admission, queue-position changes, crash recovery, and both adapters

why: Forge runs on several repos at once can start many workers, readers and reviews together and run a Mac out of memory, stopping live services
